sources.note: Scholarship regulation: Faculty/LSRI 'All'; applicable programmes PhD, DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD, DHSc; selection by alignment with strategic objectives
Scholarship page: any student offered a place in a doctoral programme is considered; faculties, institutes and research centres run the selection
PhD page: alphabetical list of 101 PhD subjects
PhD Subject Area Policy: table of 106 PhD subject areas with faculty or institute
International students: PhD at the domestic fee rate
List of the six doctoral degrees

subject_rule: Open to any subject: the scholarship covers all faculties and research institutes and any student offered a doctoral place is considered, but awards are made by each faculty, institute or centre on alignment with the university's and the unit's strategic objectives and its published selection criteria, so a subject is not guaranteed funding.

notes: Doctorate: 114 rows recorded: 109 PhD subject areas plus the 5 other named doctorates (DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD, DHSc).

The PhD page lists 101 subjects (it says over 100) and the PhD Subject Area Policy table lists 106 subject areas. The two lists differ: the policy table has Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Spanish as separate areas (the PhD page folds languages into Asian Languages and Cultures and European Languages and Culture); the PhD page has Communication, Counselling and Global Studies, which the policy table lacks. Rows combine both lists (policy names, with the PhD page names noted where they differ), so a few entries overlap in meaning (for example Asian Studies and the Asian languages).
Faculty or institute per subject is from the policy table; the three subjects only on the PhD page have no faculty stated.
International students can hold this scholarship only for the PhD, because only the PhD is charged at the domestic fee for them; the five other doctorates are for domestic students.
Programme lists were read through the web fetch tool, which returns text rather than the raw page; the policy table could not be saved as a file because the site refuses plain downloads.

Faculties, institutes and centres that run selection: Arts and Education, Auckland Bioengineering Institute, Business and Economics, Engineering and Design, Law, Liggins Institute, Medical and Health Sciences, Science, plus university research centres (Centre for Brain Research, CCREATE-AGE, MAPIHI, Nga Ara Whetu, Te Aka Matauranga Matepukupuku, Te Poutoko Ora a Kiwa, James Henare Research Centre).
not_stated: Which subjects each faculty prioritises: this sits in each faculty's own selection criteria pages, which were not read.
The page does not give a number of scholarships or a quota per subject.
fetch_problems: The university site returned an error to a plain file download (HTTP 406), so pages were read through the web fetch tool only.
The faculty selection-criteria pages (which may name priority subject areas) were not opened.
